chapter: Wooden Joe's band and Sidney Correa
title: Sidney Correa and the bands they played in together
summary: Vincent recalls playing a long time with Sidney Correa, whose brother was a classical player, and tries to name the band, settling on trombonist Raymond Brown. Mixed bands of neighbours were common.

story.theme_name: Who was in the band: naming sidemen and personnel
story.community_name: Who played in the band: reciting personnel

blocks.x: So how about Sidney Correa? Sidney used to play soccer and...

Clowness. He was a musician. Look at him, too. We used to play together. We played together a long time. And he's got a brother. His brother is... Wilde played. Played all classical music. And he's got a brother. His brother is Wilde played. Played all classical music. Professor, you know. He's a cripple. One leg short and the other. And then Sidney got a neck to play a drum. I don't think of his name. Ask him what band was it that he and Sidney worked together in. He said, what band was it that you and Sidney worked together in? Let me see what band like that. Let me see what band like that. Praera Hatise. What's your name, Brian?

Trombone player. He got his son playing trumpet. He come home one night off his job, and he got hungry, and he got some fried, fried, hot potato, and he didn't eat any gestures. Raymond Brown, that's it, man. You remember him, eh? Yeah, I believe I do. Yeah, that was an ensemble. See, when we used to play some time, we used to play all mixed up bands. They'd send me, even send me, they'd live up there, you know, up in Coralton, in the same block. And they'd get a job, and they'd get punished, but they wanted to play with him like that. Damn. The air's got... You want to turn it off on me? No, let's not let it go. What about the bass?
Yeah, the bass got... You want to turn it off on me?
No, let's not let it go.
